purpose: Phase-8A adaptive-resistance model. Adaptive resistance is a TREATMENT-INDUCED change that develops during exposure and may remain reversible. Every adaptive state must carry a documented abstract mechanism category (compensatory pathway / survival-signaling / stress-response / apoptosis-threshold / altered target dependence / altered availability / microenvironment-supported) - there is NO unexplained adaptive resistance. Each state defines a bounded sensitivity-reduction modifier, reversibility, and evidence. Schematic; no fold-resistance or IC50 shift (NOT_REPORTED).

coefficient_policy.0_interpretation: 0 = no adaptive reduction in treatment sensitivity
coefficient_policy.1_interpretation: 1 = maximal schematic adaptive reduction the model represents
coefficient_policy.source: general adaptive/non-genetic resistance biology applied predictively (no direct adaptive-resistance dataset in the frozen package)
coefficient_policy.sensitivity_note: the reduction modifier is applied to treatment sensitivity through a bounded adapter; it never edits upstream signaling/apoptosis values directly.
coefficient_policy.limitations: No fold-resistance / IC50 shift / pathway activation level (all NOT_REPORTED).

initiating.meaning: Adaptive response beginning under treatment pressure.

maintained.meaning: Adaptive resistance sustained under continued pressure.

declining.meaning: Adaptive resistance declining after pressure reduction.

rules.requires_mechanism: An adaptive state above 'absent' must reference a mechanism_category; unexplained adaptive resistance is rejected by validation.
rules.reversible_by_default: Adaptive resistance is treatment-induced and reversible unless a profile-supported persistence transition promotes it to acquired resistance.
rules.no_direct_from_absent_to_established: ABSENT may only enter INITIATING; single-frame jumps to ESTABLISHED/PERSISTENT are illegal (see resistance-transition registry).
